ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, the solenoid is connected to the resistor R, and the magnet is released from rest directly above the solenoid and passes downward through the solenoid. When the magnet has just left the solenoid, what is the relationship between its acceleration and the acceleration due to gravity?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The acceleration of the magnet just as it leaves the solenoid is less than the acceleration due to gravity
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the magnet is located directly above the solenoid, with the upper end of the magnet labeled S and the lower end labeled N; below is a vertically placed solenoid, and the right side of the solenoid is connected by wires to the resistor R to form a closed circuit. On the right side, the upper end is also labeled b and the lower end a. The problem states that the magnet is released from rest from above and passes downward through the solenoid along the axis of the solenoid. Reasoning: When the magnet has just left the solenoid, the magnetic flux between the magnet and the solenoid is still changing, so an induced current will be generated in the closed loop. According to Lenz's law, the magnetic field produced by the induced current always obstructs the relative motion that causes the change in magnetic flux; at this time the magnet is moving downward away from the solenoid, so the direction of the magnetic force exerted by the solenoid on the magnet is upward, obstructing it from continuing to fall. The magnet is subjected to gravity mg downward and, at the same time, to the induced magnetic force upward, so the downward resultant force is less than mg. Conclusion: When the magnet has just left the solenoid, the magnitude of its acceleration is less than the acceleration due to gravity g.
